title: Self-Supervised Weight Templates for Scalable Vision Model Initialization
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Prior pre-training yields separate task- and size-specific models; ours learns one shared template that is cheaply rescaled to any task or size.
layout: 2 stacked panels, top-to-bottom contrast, left-to-right flow, dashed divider
description: The figure has two stacked panels separated by a dashed line. Panel (a), "Traditional Pre-training", shows three rounded boxes for image classification, object detection and semantic segmentation. Each box has example photos (dog, bird, flower, bridge) with an arrow labeled Pre-Train pointing down to a row of layer blocks. The blocks are pink with 12 layers, green with 4 layers and yellow with 10 layers. A red wrench icon and the red caption "Task-specific, Size-specific Pre-training" sit below. Panel (b), "Constraint-based Pre-training", starts at the left with a Vision Datasets box (cat and panda photos). A self-supervised pre-train arrow leads to a stacked grid labeled Weight Templates. Colored arrows fan out to three Weight Scaler boxes (pink, green, yellow) with matrix glyphs. Each scaler feeds a task dataset card and then the layer stack of a different size. A blue puzzle icon and the caption "Task-agnostic, Size-agnostic Pre-training" close the panel.
caption: (a) Traditional pre-training paradigms produce fixed-size, task-specific models, which are difficult to adapt to downstream architectures with varying scales and task requirements. (b) SWEET adopts a constraint-based pre-training paradigm that extracts weight templates under structured constraints in a self-supervised manner, enabling flexible cross-scale and cross-task model initialization and efficient knowledge transfer.
abstract: The increasing scale and complexity of modern model parameters underscore the importance of pre-trained models. However, deployment often demands architectures of varying sizes, exposing limitations of conventional pre-training and fine-tuning. To address this, we propose SWEET, a self-supervised framework that performs constraint-based pre-training to enable scalable initialization in vision tasks. Instead of pre-training a fixed-size model, we learn a shared weight template and size-specific weight scalers under Tucker-based factorization, which promotes modularity and supports flexible adaptation to architectures with varying depths and widths. Target models are subsequently initialized by composing and reweighting the template through lightweight weight scalers, whose parameters can be efficiently learned from minimal training data. To further enhance flexibility in width expansion, we introduce width-wise stochastic scaling, which regularizes the template along width-related dimensions and encourages robust, width-invariant representations for improved cross-width generalization. Extensive experiments on \textsc{classification}, \textsc{detection}, \textsc{segmentation} and \textsc{generation} tasks demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of SWEET for initializing variable-sized vision models.
